cohort: The study included 230 pregnant women who delivered at Shalamar Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, between January 2023 and December 2024, divided into groups with preeclampsia only, GDM only, or both conditions.
finding: The co-occurrence of preeclampsia and GDM significantly worsened both maternal and neonatal outcomes, including higher rates of cesarean section, preterm birth, NICU admission, neonatal hypoglycemia, maternal ICU admission, and postpartum hemorrhage, compared to either condition alone.
mod_finding: The coexistence of preeclampsia and GDM was associated with the highest rate of cesarean section (82.7%).
